# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.

content.content:
# Change the sheet's today. Validate first so a bad date is a 400 and writes nothing.
validate:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.sheet.ValidateToday
  next: snapshot
# Keep the figures as they were, so the change can audit the ones it moves.
snapshot:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.rollup.SnapshotRollup
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: record-snapshot
# A changed today writes each person's due-total on the day being left, before it takes effect.
record-snapshot:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.rollup.RecordSnapshot
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: apply
apply:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.sheet.ApplyToday
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: autoclose
# Once the new today is set, close the periods past their grace days, before the rollup lines.
autoclose:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.period.AutoClosePeriods
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: rollup
# After the change's own lines: a line per person whose figures moved, then the totals if they did.
rollup:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.rollup.RecordRollup
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond
respond:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.sheet.RespondWithSheet
  govern: [ transaction ]
package net.officefloor.hq.app.rollup;

/** The sheet's figures as they were before the change. */
public record RollupBefore(String sheetId, Snapshot snapshot) {
}
package net.officefloor.hq.app.rollup;

import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.util.Map;

/** Every person's figures on a sheet at one moment, keyed by person id in the order they were
 *  added, and the sheet's totals. A due-total is null when it is n/a. An overdue-total is the dues of
 *  the counting OPEN (or PENDING) claims whose due-by is before the sheet's today (n/a ones skipped). */
public record Snapshot(Map<Long, PersonFigures> people, BigDecimal claimedTotal, BigDecimal dueTotal, BigDecimal overdueTotal) {

    public record PersonFigures(String name, BigDecimal claimed, BigDecimal dueTotal, BigDecimal overdueTotal) {
    }
}
package net.officefloor.hq.app.rollup;

import net.officefloor.plugin.variable.Out;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PathVariable;

/** Runs before the change: keeps the sheet's figures as they were. */
public class SnapshotRollup {
    public void snapshot(@PathVariable("sheetId") String sheetId, Rollup rollup, Out<RollupBefore> before) {
        before.set(new RollupBefore(sheetId, rollup.snapshot(sheetId)));
    }
}

content.text:
Each person now shows their snapshot lines, oldest first, in the form `<the day being left> <due-total>`, with `n/a` when the due-total was n/a. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it works:**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V79__person_snapshot.sql`, adds a `person_snapshot` table holding the sheet, the person, the day being left and the due-total. It follows the same pattern as the other per-person tables, so it is also kept in the as-of history. I added it to `AsOf.TABLES` so the as-of view can read it.
- **Server:** `RecordSnapshot` already wrote one `SNAPSHOT` audit line per person when the sheet's today moves. It now also saves a matching row for each person, using the today in force before the change as the day being left. The audit lines themselves are unchanged.
- **Person data:** `People` reads the snapshot lines for each person, and `PersonResponse` sends them to the front end as a new `snapshots` list.
- **Front end:** a new `features/snapshots/snapshots.slot.tsx` adds a "Snapshots" column to the person row, with one `person-snapshot-line` element per line.

When a person is merged into someone else or transferred to another sheet, their snapshot lines are deleted along with their other per-person data. They are not carried over to the person or sheet they end up on, and cloning a sheet doesn't copy them either.
